question_text:
A cylindrical bar of aluminum 19 mm ( 0.75 in.) in diameter is to be deformed elastically by application of a force along the bar axis. Using the data in  table 7.1 , determine the force that produces an elastic reduction of $2.5 \times$ $10^{-3} \mathrm{~mm}\left(1.0 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{in}\right.$.) in the diameter.

Reference:
"Table 7.1 Room-Temperature Elastic and Shear Moduli and Poisson's Ratio for Various Materials
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \multirow[b]{2}{*}{Material} & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Modulus of Elasticity} & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Shear Modulus} & \multirow[b]{2}{*}{Poisson's Ratio} \\
\hline & GPa & $10^6 \mathrm{psi}$ & GPa & $10^6 \mathrm{psi}$ & \\
\hline \multicolumn{6}{|c|}{Metal Alloys} \\
\hline Tungsten & 407 & 59 & 160 & 23.2 & 0.28 \\
\hline Steel & 207 & 30 & 83 & 12.0 & 0.30 \\
\hline Nickel & 207 & 30 & 76 & 11.0 & 0.31 \\
\hline Titanium & 107 & 15.5 & 45 & 6.5 & 0.34 \\
\hline Copper & 110 & 16 & 46 & 6.7 & 0.34 \\
\hline Brass & 97 & 14 & 37 & 5.4 & 0.34 \\
\hline Aluminum & 69 & 10 & 25 & 3.6 & 0.33 \\
\hline Magnesium & 45 & 6.5 & 17 & 2.5 & 0.35 \\
\hline \multicolumn{6}{|c|}{Ceramic Materials} \\
\hline Aluminum oxide ( $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ ) & 393 & 57 & - & - & 0.22 \\
\hline Silicon carbide ( SiC ) & 345 & 50 & - & - & 0.17 \\
\hline Silicon nitride ( $\mathrm{Si}_3 \mathrm{~N}_4$ ) & 304 & 44 & - & - & 0.30 \\
\hline Spinel ( $\mathrm{MgAl}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$ ) & 260 & 38 & - & - & - \\
\hline Magnesium oxide (MgO) & 225 & 33 & - & - & 0.18 \\
\hline Zirconia $\left(\mathrm{ZrO}_2\right)^a$ & 205 & 30 & - & - & 0.31 \\
\hline Mullite ( $3 \mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3-2 \mathrm{SiO}_2$ ) & 145 & 21 & - & - & 0.24 \\
\hline Glass-ceramic (Pyroceram) & 120 & 17 & - & - & 0.25 \\
\hline Fused silica ( $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ ) & 73 & 11 & - & - & 0.17 \\
\hline Soda-lime glass & 69 & 10 & - & - & 0.23 \\
\hline \multicolumn{6}{|c|}{Polymers ${ }^{\text {b }}$} \\
\hline Phenol-formaldehyde & 2.76-4.83 & 0.40-0.70 & - & - & - \\
\hline Poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) & 2.41-4.14 & 0.35-0.60 & - & - & 0.38 \\
\hline Poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) & 2.76-4.14 & 0.40-0.60 & - & - & 0.33 \\
\hline Polystyrene (PS) & 2.28-3.28 & 0.33-0.48 & - & - & 0.33 \\

\hline Polypropylene (PP) & 1.14-1.55 & 0.17-0.23 & - & - & 0.40 \\
\hline Polyethylene-high density (HDPE) & 1.08 & 0.16 & - & - & 0.46 \\

response:
## Step-by-Step Reasoning

**Given data (Aluminum, from Table 7.1):**
- Modulus of elasticity: $E = 69 \text{ GPa}$
- Poisson's ratio: $\nu = 0.33$
- Original diameter: $d_0 = 19 \text{ mm}$
- Diameter reduction: $\Delta d = 2.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mm}$

**1. Lateral (transverse) strain:**

The reduction in diameter is a lateral strain:
$$\varepsilon_x = \frac{\Delta d}{d_0} = \frac{2.5\times10^{-3}}{19} = 1.316\times10^{-4}$$

**2. Relate lateral strain to axial strain via Poisson's ratio:**

By definition, $\varepsilon_x = -\nu\,\varepsilon_z$, so the axial tensile strain is:
$$\varepsilon_z = \frac{\varepsilon_x}{\nu} = \frac{1.316\times10^{-4}}{0.33} = 3.99\times10^{-4}$$

**3. Axial stress (Hooke's law):**
$$\sigma = E\,\varepsilon_z = (69\times10^{9})(3.99\times10^{-4}) \approx 2.75\times10^{7} \text{ Pa}$$

**4. Force = stress × cross-sectional area:**
$$A = \frac{\pi d_0^2}{4} = \frac{\pi(0.019)^2}{4} = 2.835\times10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$$

$$F = \sigma A \approx (2.75\times10^{7})(2.835\times10^{-4}) \approx 7800 \text{ N}$$

$$\boxed{7800}$$
